2027-07-01.title: Thursday of the sixth week after Pentecost · Aaron the High Priest
readings: Every high priest is chosen from among mortals and takes the honour only when called by God, just as Aaron was
Zechariah the priest and Elizabeth, a descendant of Aaron; the whole assembly prays outside at the hour of incense
2027-07-01.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers today Aaron the High Priest (പ്രധാനാചാര്യനായ അഹറോൻ), the brother of Moses, the first to hold the priestly office of Israel. Today is also the first day of July, which the Syriac calendar calls Tammuz (തോമ്മൂസ്).
2027-07-01.verse: And one does not presume to take this honor, but takes it only when called by God, just as Aaron was.
theo: Today is the first day of July, the Syriac month of Tammuz, and the Panchangam begins it by remembering a priest: Aaron, the brother of Moses and the first High Priest of Israel. He did not push himself forward. The Epistle says so plainly: “And one does not presume to take this honor, but takes it only when called by God, just as Aaron was.” At Sinai the Lord said to Moses: “Then bring near to you your brother Aaron, and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests.” The calling came first; the vestments, the oil and the altar followed. And the vestments themselves carried a lesson. On the shoulders of the High Priest were two stones engraved with the names of the sons of Israel: “Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord on his two shoulders for remembrance.” On the breastpiece over his heart were the same names, “for a continual remembrance before the Lord.” A priest in the Bible is never a man standing alone. He carries a whole people on his shoulders and on his heart.

Then the Epistle says something that may surprise us. The high priest “is able to deal gently with the ignorant and wayward, since he himself is subject to weakness; and because of this he must offer sacrifice for his own sins as well as for those of the people.” Aaron's own story shows it. While Moses was on the mountain, the people gathered around Aaron and asked him to make gods for them, and he fashioned a golden calf (Exodus 32:1–4). When Moses questioned him, Aaron answered with excuses (Exodus 32:21–24). The Bible does not hide the failing of its first High Priest. Yet the same Aaron, when a plague broke out in the camp, took his censer at the word of Moses and ran into the middle of the assembly, and the text says: “He stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stopped.” A sinner standing between death and life with incense in his hand: that is the picture of a priest. God himself confirmed the choice when the leaders of the tribes laid their staffs before him, and “the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted. It put forth buds, produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.” At the end, on Mount Hor, Moses placed Aaron's vestments on his son Eleazar, so that the priesthood passed on (Numbers 20:25–28).

All of this was a shadow, and the Letter to the Hebrews shows where the light falls. Aaron had to offer sacrifice for his own sins before he could offer it for others. Jesus Christ, our great High Priest, “has been tested as we are, yet without sin,” so that we may “approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need” (Hebrews 4:15–16). The sacrifices of the old covenant had to be repeated again and again; of Christ the letter says that he “has no need to offer sacrifices day after day, first for his own sins, and then for those of the people; this he did once for all when he offered himself” (Hebrews 7:27). The Church therefore does not think of her priests as men who add something to the one sacrifice of the Cross. They serve in the name and in the person of Christ, so that the one offering made once for all is made present on the altar for every generation (Catechism 1545, in substance). We thank God for our bishops, priests and deacons, and we ask ourselves how often we pray for them by name.

St Luke begins his Gospel inside this very priesthood. “In the days of King Herod of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly order of Abijah. His wife was a descendant of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.” Aaron's line, after more than a thousand years, has reached the threshold of the New Testament. Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous, advanced in years and without a child. Zechariah “was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and offer incense.” Then Luke adds a sentence that is easy to miss: “Now at the time of the incense offering, the whole assembly of the people was praying outside.” The priest is inside, the people are outside, and the smoke of the incense rises between them, as the psalmist had prayed: “Let my prayer be counted as incense before you” (Psalm 141:2). It is at that hour of prayer, in that meeting of priest and people, that the angel appears and the new age begins. The same shape is in every Holy Qurbono: the priest at the altar, the people in prayer, the incense rising, and heaven opening above them. As the month begins, let us pray that our priests may be faithful to the call by which God took them from among us, and let us not stay outside the church even when we sit inside it, but pray with them.
outline: Ask: when did I last pray for a priest by name, and when did I last thank one?
Aaron did not take the honour for himself; the Lord brought him near, and Christ says the same to his Apostles.
Point 2 · A priest who knows weakness
The golden calf, and the censer between the dead and the living: God works through a sinner who stands for the people.
Aaron offered for his own sins first; Jesus, tested yet without sin, offered himself once for all.
Point 4 · The incense and the people outside
Zechariah inside, the whole assembly praying outside: the prayer of the people rises with the priest's offering.
“He stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stopped.”
live: Name one priest or bishop who has served you and pray for him by name each day this week; thank him in person or by a message.
Write down five names you want to carry before God, as Aaron carried the names of the tribes, and offer them in prayer at the next Holy Qurbono.
Fix one hour each evening this week, when the lamp is lit at home, for a few quiet minutes of prayer with the family.
2027-07-01.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, great High Priest, tested as we are yet without sin, you offered yourself once for all and you ever live to make intercession for us. We thank you for Aaron, whom you called from among his people to stand before you with their names on his heart, and we ask that you keep our bishops, priests and deacons faithful to the call by which you took them from among us. Make them gentle with the ignorant and the wayward, since they too are subject to weakness. Let our prayer rise before you like incense, and let none of your people stay outside when your holy mysteries are celebrated. At the beginning of this new month bless our homes and our parish, and bring us at last to the sanctuary of heaven, where you live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the priest stands at the altar before God for the people, with the censer, the bread and the wine; he does not act in his own name but in the name of Christ, the one High Priest, whose single offering on the Cross is made present for us, and the incense that rises is the prayer of the whole assembly.
conn: Exodus 28:1 and Hebrews 5:4: Aaron is brought near by the Lord and does not take the honour himself; John 15:16: “You did not choose me but I chose you.” The call always comes first from God.

Exodus 28:12 and 28:29: the names of the tribes on the shoulders and over the heart of the High Priest; Psalm 133:2 pictures the anointing oil running down from the head of Aaron over his robes, a sign of blessing flowing down on a whole community living in unity.

Exodus 30:7–8: fragrant incense offered by Aaron morning and evening; Luke 1:9–10: the people pray outside while Zechariah offers incense; Psalm 141:2 and Revelation 8:3–4: the prayers of the saints rise with the incense before God.
fathers: The priestly office is carried out on earth, but it ranks among heavenly things, for it was not a man or an angel but the Paraclete himself who established this ministry (On the Priesthood 3.4, in substance).

For you I am a bishop, with you I am a Christian: the first is a duty that I accept, the second a grace that I receive; the priest is a servant of God's people and at the same time one of them (Sermon 340.1, in substance).
magis: The Lord set the tribe of Levi apart for the liturgical service of Israel and consecrated Aaron and his sons by a special rite; yet that priesthood could not bring about salvation and had to repeat its sacrifices without end, awaiting the sacrifice of Christ that would sanctify once for all (in substance).

Everything that the priesthood of the old covenant foreshadowed is fulfilled in Christ, the one mediator between God and humankind; his one priesthood is made present through the ministerial priesthood without diminishing the uniqueness of Christ's priesthood (in substance).

The common priesthood of the faithful and the ministerial priesthood of the ordained differ in essence and not only in degree, yet they are ordered one to the other; each in its own way shares in the one priesthood of Christ (in substance).

quick: The Epistle says that no one takes the honour of the priesthood for himself: he is called by God, just as Aaron was.
The high priest can deal gently with sinners because he too is subject to weakness; Jesus, tested yet without sin, is the great High Priest who offered himself once for all.
In the Gospel Zechariah offers incense while the whole assembly prays outside; Elizabeth is a descendant of Aaron.
2027-07-01.action: Pray today by name for one priest or bishop, and thank God for the call by which he was taken from among us.
2027-07-01.question: Do I pray with my priest when I am in church, or do I stay outside while I sit inside?

family.explain: A priest is a person God chooses to be a special helper for his people. Aaron was the first High Priest, the brother of Moses. He wore beautiful clothes with twelve shining stones on his chest, and on each stone was the name of one family of Israel, so that wherever he went he carried the people with him. Zechariah, in our Gospel, was a priest who came from the family of Aaron. While he offered incense, the people were outside praying. Priests and people pray together, and Jesus is the greatest High Priest of all.
family.intention: We pray for our priests and bishops, and for the sacristans, altar servers and choir who help us to pray.
family.ask: Ask: “Which priest taught you something about Jesus? Let us say a prayer for him now.”

illus: In a hill parish in Idukki the old sacristan had lit the charcoal for the censer every Sunday for forty years. During the monsoon the charcoal was damp and often refused to light, and on such mornings he would crouch at the back of the sacristy with a bundle of dry coconut husk, blowing patiently. A young deacon once asked him why he took such trouble, since the priest could surely begin the Qurbono without incense. The old man replied that the incense was not his and not the priest's either; it was the prayer of everyone outside the sanctuary rising to God, and his only work was to keep the fire alive so that the people's prayer would have somewhere to go. Years later that deacon, now a priest, said that whenever he swung the censer he remembered the old man crouching with the damp charcoal, and prayed for the people whose prayers it carried.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, great High Priest, you carry your people before the Father. Teach us to pray with our priests and to pray for them, and let our prayer rise before you like incense. Amen.
share: No one presumes to take this honour, but takes it only when called by God, just as Aaron was (Hebrews 5:4). Who first showed me the meaning of a call from God?
He stood between the dead and the living (Numbers 16:48). Where am I asked to stand between a troubled person and God, by prayer or by presence?
The whole assembly of the people was praying outside (Luke 1:10). Do I take part in the prayer of the Church, or do I watch it?
pm.resp: Lord, hear the prayer of your people.
interc: For our bishops, priests and deacons, that they may be faithful to the call of God and gentle with the weak.
For vocations to the priesthood and the religious life in our eparchies and parishes.
For those who serve in the sacristy and at the altar, for the choir and the servers, that their service may be offered with love.
For parishes without a priest of their own, and for priests who are sick, lonely or discouraged.
For all of us, that our prayer may rise like incense and our lives may be a pleasing offering.
pm.close: Father, you called Aaron from among his people and in your Son you gave us a High Priest who has no sin. Keep your priests close to your heart, keep your people faithful in prayer, and gather us all around your altar. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The Hebrew title is kohen gadol, “the great priest”, and the Letter to the Hebrews uses the Greek word archiereus. It means the chief of the priests, who alone entered the holy of holies once a year; the Letter shows that Jesus Christ is the one true High Priest.
kidsaint: Some people in the camp of Israel complained and asked who had really been chosen to be priest. God told Moses to take twelve wooden staffs, one for each tribe, and to place them in the tent before the Lord overnight. In the morning the staff with Aaron's name had sprouted! It had buds and flowers and even ripe almonds. Now everyone knew whom God had chosen. Lesson: God is the one who calls, and he gives his helpers what they need to serve.

homily: Dear friends, today is the first day of July, and the Panchangam begins the month by remembering Aaron the High Priest, the brother of Moses. The Letter to the Hebrews says that no one takes the honour of the priesthood for himself: one takes it only when called by God, just as Aaron was (Hebrews 5:4). God brought Aaron near and gave him vestments with the names of the twelve tribes on his shoulders and over his heart, so that he would never forget the people he served.

Aaron was not perfect. The Epistle says that a high priest is subject to weakness and must offer sacrifice for his own sins as well as for those of the people (Hebrews 5:2–3). Aaron made the golden calf. Yet when the plague came he took his censer and ran into the middle of the assembly, and he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped (Numbers 16:48). God works through weak people who stand for the others.

Jesus Christ is the great High Priest who was tested as we are, yet without sin (Hebrews 4:15). He offered himself once for all (Hebrews 7:27). Every priest who serves at our altar serves in his name. In the Gospel Zechariah, a priest of Aaron's line, offers incense, and the whole assembly of the people is praying outside (Luke 1:10). The priest and the people pray together.
So today let us pray for our bishops, priests and deacons by name, and let us pray with them at every Holy Qurbono, so that our prayer rises like incense. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what a priest is? A priest is a person whom God chooses to be a special helper for his people. A long time ago Aaron, the brother of Moses, was the first High Priest. He wore a beautiful breastpiece with twelve stones, and on every stone there was a name, so that he carried all the families of Israel on his heart. Today our priests also carry us on their hearts. Say a little prayer for your parish priest today, and when you see him, say thank you!

intro: Theme: “And one does not presume to take this honor, but takes it only when called by God, just as Aaron was.”
On Thursday of the sixth week after Pentecost, the memory of Aaron the High Priest: the call of God, the priest who knows weakness, the one High Priest, and the prayer that rises like incense.

sub: Aaron was brought near by the Lord.
No one takes the honour for himself.
The names of the people on his shoulders and heart.
q: Then bring near to you your brother Aaron, and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests
You did not choose me but I chose you.
points.apply: Thank God for the call by which one priest was taken from among us, and pray for him by name this week.

sub: The golden calf and the excuses.
The censer between the dead and the living.
q: He stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stopped.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: When you see the failing of a priest or of anyone who serves, pray for him before you judge him.

sub: The prayers of the saints in golden bowls.
q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
points.apply: At the next Holy Qurbono, when the incense rises, offer to God the names of those you carry in prayer.

concl: God calls his priests from among the people, and he works through them in spite of their weakness, because the one High Priest is Jesus Christ.
The prayer of the people rises with the priest's offering; no one in the church should stay outside.
2027-07-01.resolve: Pray for your priests by name, pray with them at the altar, and let your prayer rise like incense.
